locator: I q.4 a.2 co.: Omnium autem perfectiones pertinent ad perfectionem essendi: secundum hoc enim aliqua perfecta sunt, quod aliquo modo esse habent
interpretation: From the second proof (God as ipsum esse subsistens): the perfections of all things pertain to the perfection of being, since things are perfect insofar as they have being in some way. Kept as prose, not formalized; it supports the open bridge STMT-CAUSE-OF-BEING-CAUSES-EVERY-PERFECTION, which adds the causal step that the cause of a thing's being causes what pertains to its being. Re-read the full pinned article in the causal-transfer investigation: the second proof specifically invokes subsistent esse; ad 3 distinguishes participation in being from participation in every mode. Neither this claim nor the first proof’s preexistence establishes causal responsibility for each particular actuality. Detailed boundaries: docs/notes/causal-perfection-transfer.md.
